review: authored-from-existing-guide; extraction only, not independent verification

The Trinsic Murders.gentle: Start with the crime scene and compare the witnesses' accounts. Report what you can establish before trying to leave town.
The Trinsic Murders.balanced: Examine the stables, speak with Spark and Gilberto, then report your findings to Mayor Finnigan.

Infiltrating the Fellowship.gentle: Keep track of the errands you accept and return to the person who assigned them.
Infiltrating the Fellowship.balanced: Batlin in Britain asks for a delivery to Elynor in Minoc. The guide also describes a 9 PM service and a Destard errand, but its sources disagree on their order.
Infiltrating the Fellowship.conflict: Fellowship errand and meeting order differs between DB, OFFLINE_HINTS, and the old prompt. No sequencing prerequisite is asserted.

The Quest for the Time Lord.gentle: Listen to the forest's inhabitants and consider what might earn their trust.
The Quest for the Time Lord.balanced: Bring honey from the Bee Cave to the emps in the Deep Forest, then ask about communicating with the wisp.

The Answers to Life and Death.gentle: Listen to the island's troubled inhabitants and investigate what keeps them from finding peace.
The Answers to Life and Death.balanced: Speak with the spirits of Skara Brae. The guide connects their troubles to Horance and the Well of Souls.
The Answers to Life and Death.conflict: DB describes Seance as travel; its spells entry describes speaking with spirits. Travel mechanism omitted.

Destroying the Guardian's Generators.gentle: Each obstacle calls for its own preparation. Consult the people studying the unusual disturbances.
Destroying the Guardian's Generators.balanced: The guide pairs the Tetrahedron with the Ethereal Ring, the Sphere with Nicodemus's Hourglass, and the Cube with Caddellite protection.

The Isle of the Avatar and Final Battle.gentle: Review the special objects gathered during the investigation before entering the final site.
The Isle of the Avatar and Final Battle.balanced: The three generator prisms have a purpose at the Black Gate. Consult the direct solution for their placement and the final tool.

How to get to the Isle of Fire.gentle: Ask the ruler about the recent disturbances and the means to investigate them.
How to get to the Isle of Fire.balanced: Speak to Lord British about the tremors. The guide describes a ship at Vesper and a landing on the isle's north side.
aliases: get to the Isle of Fire
how to reach the Isle of Fire

Doors are broken?.gentle: A closed door alone does not establish a bug. Keep a separate save and compare what you have tried with the guide's described route.
Doors are broken?.balanced: The guide reports a possible Castle of Fire door problem, but this assistant cannot verify its cause or your game version. Preserve your current save before testing an earlier one.
Doors are broken?.conflict: Cause, version applicability, and cheat recovery not independently verified. No automatic bug diagnosis.

Castle of Fire.gentle: Explore the inhabited rooms and speak to the castle's resident before starting the tests.
Castle of Fire.balanced: Erethian in the west wing explains the Tests and the Shrine of Principles.

Test of Truth.gentle: Treat the test's name as a warning about appearances. Examine what you passed before committing to the maze.
Test of Truth.balanced: The guide places the true solution before the labyrinth. Reconsider the clue about a hood and the direction north.

Test of Love.gentle: Read the instructions near those who need help. Consider whether completing one act leaves another unfinished.
Test of Love.balanced: The Stone of Castambre ritual must help both Bollux and Adjhar; the guide describes performing it twice.

Test of Courage.gentle: Prepare for several types of enemy, and examine the rooms between fights.
Test of Courage.balanced: Sleep potions help against dragons. Search carefully for equipment and inspect the helmet pedestal puzzle.

Forging the Black Sword.gentle: Ask the castle's resident about the unfinished artifact, then inspect the tools around it.
Forging the Black Sword.balanced: The forge needs repeated heating and hammering. The guide links the blade's completion to the Ether Gem and Arcadion.

Finale.gentle: Return to unfinished business and review the objects earned from the tests.
Finale.balanced: Complete the remaining Courage encounter, then assemble the lenses and Talismans of Principle at the Dark Core.

Free Weston!.gentle: Hear the prisoner's account and seek someone with the authority to review his case.
Free Weston!.balanced: Speak to Weston in Castle British's jail, then bring his case to Lord British.

Who Stole the Poison?.gentle: Compare accounts and look for physical evidence before accusing anyone.
Who Stole the Poison?.balanced: Begin with Morfin in Paws. The sources disagree about the key and chest details, so the assistant cannot give a reliable search route.
Who Stole the Poison?.conflict: DB says Garritt's chest; OFFLINE_HINTS and prompt describe a Shelter chest and multiple keys. Search route quarantined.

Where Does Patterson go at Night?.gentle: Observe the person's routine after the evening gathering.
Where Does Patterson go at Night?.balanced: Attend the 9 PM Fellowship meeting in Britain, then follow Patterson discreetly.

Miranda's Law.gentle: Check who needs to sign the document and who expects it back.
Miranda's Law.balanced: Take Miranda's bill from Britain to Lord Heather in Cove, then return the signed bill.

Nastassia's Father.gentle: Ask people who knew the missing person's travels, then bring the news home.
Nastassia's Father.balanced: Ask the emps in the Deep Forest, particularly Trellek, about Julius.

Owen the Shipwright, Hero or Fraud?.gentle: An accusation needs evidence and someone qualified to interpret it.
Owen the Shipwright, Hero or Fraud?.balanced: Find the ship plans and have an experienced tinker assess them before presenting the evidence to the mayor.

The Honor Flag.gentle: Hear the dispute carefully. A practical replacement may offer an alternative to fighting.
The Honor Flag.balanced: Sprellic needs help in Jhelom. You can champion his duels or ask Kliftin about a replica flag.

Blorn's Accusations.gentle: Hear both sides before accepting the accusation.
Blorn's Accusations.balanced: Speak to Lap-Lem as well as Blorn, and ask about the disputed amulet.

Where does Catherine Go?.gentle: Quiet observation may reveal more than a confrontation.
Where does Catherine Go?.balanced: Observe Catherine around noon and follow without interrupting her.

Balayna's Doubts.gentle: Consider the consequences before repeating something told to you in confidence.
Balayna's Doubts.balanced: Balayna's concerns involve Rankin. The guide warns that reporting her doubts may put her in danger.

Brion's Orrery.gentle: Ask what the device is missing, then seek someone who trades unusual objects.
Brion's Orrery.balanced: Brion needs a crystal. Ask the adventurer Addom about obtaining one.

Who wants to destroy the Shrine?.gentle: Investigate the concern and look for written evidence before confronting anyone.
Who wants to destroy the Shrine?.balanced: Begin with Teregus in Terfin and examine the evidence around the suspected plot.

Mysterious Monk.gentle: Check the stranger's story against the local records.
Mysterious Monk.balanced: Investigate Kreg's identity through Yew's court records.

Who Defaced Lord British?.gentle: Collect physical evidence and interview people who can interpret it.
Who Defaced Lord British?.balanced: Gather stone chips and blood, then consult Lady Leigh and Lady Tory.

Tory's Baby.gentle: Ask about the missing child's last known whereabouts and prepare for a rescue.
Tory's Baby.balanced: The guide points toward the Shrine of Honour and warns of harpies. Direct advice includes its coordinates.

research.title: Black Gate's identity
research.text: The Black Gate is a black moongate being built so the Guardian can enter Britannia from another dimension.

sources.label: Ultima VII dialogue transcript: Xorinia (exchange and Black Gate)

research.title: Lord British's identity
research.text: Lord British rules Britannia as its king. He is an old friend of the Avatar and shares the Avatar's original homeland, Earth.

sources.label: Ultima VII dialogue transcript: Lord British (name, job and homeland)

research.title: Guardian
research.text: In Ultima VII: The Black Gate, the Guardian is a powerful, hostile being from another dimension. He seeks domination and control of Britannia, and the Time Lord urges the Avatar to oppose him.

sources.label: Ultima VII dialogue transcript: The Time Lord (crisis and The Guardian)

research.title: Avatar
research.text: The Avatar is Britannia's champion of the Eight Virtues. In Ultima VII, Lord British recognizes the Avatar as an old friend who, like him, originally came from Earth.

sources.label: Ultima VII manual: The Book of Fellowship (the Eight Virtues and the Quest of the Avatar)
Ultima VII dialogue transcript: Lord British (homeland)

research.title: Britannia
research.text: Britannia is the realm ruled by Lord British, where the Avatar returns in Ultima VII: The Black Gate. It is a different world from Earth, the original homeland of Lord British and the Avatar.

sources.label: Ultima VII dialogue transcript: Lord British (job, homeland and Britannia)

research.title: Guardian's goal
research.text: The Guardian wants power and domination: he conquers other worlds and has turned his attention to Britannia.

sources.label: Ultima VII dialogue transcript: Xorinia (exchange)

research.title: Time Lord's request
research.text: The Time Lord wants the Avatar to free him and help oppose the Guardian.

sources.label: Ultima VII dialogue transcript: The Time Lord (crisis)

research.title: Time Lord and Guardian
research.text: The Time Lord and the Guardian are opponents: the Time Lord asks the Avatar to fight the Guardian, who has trapped him.

sources.label: Ultima VII dialogue transcript: The Time Lord (crisis)

research.title: Time Lord
research.text: In Ultima VII: The Black Gate, the Time Lord is a being whose work is to keep time flowing smoothly through space. He helps the Avatar oppose the Guardian.

sources.label: Ultima VII dialogue transcript: The Time Lord (name, job and crisis)

research.title: Gaining levels and training
research.text: Ultima VII levels arrive automatically once enough experience is earned. Each level gives three training points, which trainers turn into attribute increases; each trainer needs a minimum number of points before teaching.

sources.label: Ultima Codex: Character advancement

research.title: Curing poison and sleep
research.text: In Ultima VII, drinking a red potion cures all poisons, whereas an orange potion awakens a sleeping party member. The first-circle Cure spell (An Nox; Garlic and Ginseng) also flushes poison from an afflicted companion.

sources.label: Ultima Codex: Potions
Ultima Codex: Cure

researchReview: Outside research: authored one-to-three-sentence summaries of the cited pages, checked on the listed date. Shown with an "outside research" label; the guide’s own facts win when both exist. Not independently play-tested.

page.text: Upon leveling up, characters gain 3 training points. Spend these at trainers to increase attributes. The key is the "rubber-band effect": training a secondary skill (Combat, Magic) yields huge gains if it's far below its primary attribute (Dexterity, Intelligence).
For Fighters: Train Combat until it's 1 point higher than Dexterity. Then, train only Dexterity. This raises both stats efficiently.
For the Avatar (Mage): Raise Intelligence first to create a large gap with the Magic skill. Then train Magic for massive mana pool increases.
Training costs gold, but Britannia's economy is easily broken. Use these methods to fund your party's rapid advancement.
Infinite XP (Britain): Repeatedly accept Batlin's quest to deliver a package to Minoc without taking the second package.
Infinite XP (Buccaneer's Den): Reconcile the feuding pirates Mole and Blacktooth over and over.
Infinite Gold: Hunt green drakes in Dungeon Destard. They frequently drop diamonds, which sell for a high price to the Britain jeweler.
Free Training: Sentri in Britain offers free Dexterity training, which also boosts Combat. He is the most valuable trainer in the early game.
This expansion is essential. Completing it raises the Avatar's core stats to their maximum value, trivializing most combat. It should be a top priority.
To begin, speak to Lord British about the "rumble" felt at the start of the game. He will direct you to the newly risen Isle of Fire to undertake the three tests.
This test, located in its own dungeon on the Isle of Fire, challenges your perception and ability to see beyond illusions.
This test requires empathy and understanding to resolve a conflict within its dungeon.
The final and most combat-heavy test. You must be well-equipped and prepared to face a powerful dragon at its conclusion.

Upon completing all three tests, you will forge the mighty Black Sword. More importantly, Lord British will reward you by raising your Strength, Dexterity, and Intelligence to 30 (or even 60 in some versions). This is the single largest power boost in the game.
The Avatar leads. Add up to eight travelling companions; your plan is saved in this browser.
Recruit a balanced fellowship, secure dependable equipment, and keep Seance plus Destroy Trap ready.
Quest-critical and survival magic should take priority over spectacle.

Two centuries after the Avatar's last journey, a ritual killing reveals a conspiracy spreading beneath an age of peace. Assemble old friends, follow the Fellowship, and close the Black Gate before its master can cross.
